newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina nearly set to sign IMF deal - Fernandez.
newsitem.headline: Argentina nearly set to sign IMF deal - Fernandez.

text.p: The Argentine government is putting the final touches on a letter of intent with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that sets a 1996 budget deficit target of $5 billion, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Tuesday.
Fernandez told a news conference that the letter of intent is expected to be signed before the weekend.
The deficit target is $5 billion according to IMF calculations and $6 billion according to Argentine accounting methods, he said.

"In terms of the budget and what has really been committed in spending vis-a-vis revenues, the deficit is $6 billion," Fernandez said. He added that in Argentine terms the 1997 budget deficit target is $3 billion, meaning that Argentina's will require $12 billion in financing.
Fernandez will travel to Frankfurt, London and New York September 22-23 before attending the annual meetings of the World Bank and the IMF.
He also said that Carlos Sanchez, who served as deputy to former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, will remain the head of the DGI tax office.
"I asked Sanchez to stay in charge of the DGI," he said. Officials said last week that Sanchez was about to leave the post.
